title: Contact-conditioned lateral reflection and joint outcome diffusion
coverage_gap: All five support layouts start with the goal below the peg in world y, by roughly0.041-0.059 m, although reach directions from the hand have both signs. C/E can require the opposite transport direction and a much larger displacement. A3 explicitly folds the undercovered positive post-contact lateral direction into negative-error coordinates and learns action/outcome correlations jointly, rather than asking signed-feature regression alone to extrapolate.
reusable_regularity: Once the hand is near the grasp point with a small aperture, reversing a lateral goal error approximately reverses lateral transport without reversing gravity, insertion x, or gripper closure. Use only this partial symmetry, and retain world/asymmetry information. A ten-channel common U-Net jointly denoises encoded action4 and six future geometric-error coordinates so the diffusion model learns correlations between grasp maintenance, head alignment and actions. It does not optimize a plan or query a forward model.
dependencies_preserved: The frame is S=diag(1,s,1), not a full task-goal rotation: x insertion direction and z/table clearance stay in native axes.

Signed reflected reach, insertion and shaft vectors preserve both pegGrasp and pegHead dependencies; both native previous-step motion vectors and both whole causal observations use the same chunk-start frame.
Current and previous xyzw quaternion transform by (s*qx,qy,s*qz,qw), the axial-vector rule for S R S, so orientation remains consistent with vector reflection.

Unreflected coarse absolute hand and goal xyz, all relevant heights and explicit reflection parity preserve robot/world and obstacle placement dependencies. This allows the DP to learn deviations from ideal lateral mirror symmetry.
Aperture is never reflected and the absence of object2 is the only reason its zero channels are omitted. The box is located by the provided goal, never by a hidden box pose or simulator call.
The deterministic contact surrogate uses only current aperture and hand-to-grasp distance. It is neither a contact oracle nor an inferred action command.

evidence_refs.use: Exact five-episode evidence scope; no performance or additional task data.
Independent peg_y/box_y evaluation factors, fixed orientation, native action cube, world axes and explicit head channel.
All initial peg-to-goal y offsets negative; initial hand-to-peg y has both signs; only LL and HH demonstrations. This motivates reflection only after the contact-like stage, not during reaching.
World-constrained peg and side-opening geometry; gravity and side insertion are not arbitrary rotational symmetries.
Grasp/transport geometry differs from free reaching.
Peg carried toward the side opening with orientation largely maintained.
End geometry supports head-to-goal alignment as an outcome variable.
Near-grasp aperture falls through0.5 and hand/peg separation becomes small; transport moves pegHead as well as hand; later y overshoot motivates a5mm identity-frame deadband.
Coherent hand and head displacement during grasped transport in HH as well as LL.
Joint diffusion permits appended channels but action4 remains first and frame is fixed at causal chunk start.
Inference samples all ten channels without future truth and executes only decoded action4. Common action epsilon normalization is unchanged.

expected_failure_signature: If approximate lateral mirror symmetry is invalid because of robot or box-side interactions, previously unseen positive transport may approach the correct y but show different contact or overshoot errors than matched negative transport.

The contact surrogate can reflect a closed empty gripper; this would produce transport commands without a corresponding carried peg. A failure to recognize contact instead leaves positive transport in its unsupported native frame.
Parity changes near the5mm boundary or contact threshold can cause chunk-to-chunk y oscillation despite exact within-chunk invertibility.

Joint auxiliary diffusion may memorize the narrow support's future path and interfere with actions for longer E transports; predicted lateral outcome range would then remain too short. No such outcome or performance is claimed as observed.

action_frame_semantics.causal_frame_definition: At the current chunk start, contact=(aperture<0.5 and norm(pegGrasp-hand)<0.065m). Set s=-1 only if contact and goal_y-pegHead_y>0.005m, otherwise s=+1. This intentionally leaves reaching in native coordinates and retains a near-alignment identity deadband.
action_frame_semantics.encode: For all16 native action4 rows use [dx,s*dy,dz,gripper]. No translation, rescaling, clipping or action generation is performed.
action_frame_semantics.decode: Use the identical chunk-start s: [encoded_dx,s*encoded_dy,encoded_dz,gripper]. S squared equals I; y reflection preserves the native action cube and Euclidean translation scale. Gripper remains its scalar native command. Only the executor clips and executes the fixed four-action prefix.
action_frame_semantics.quaternion: Reflection is a coordinate mapping, not an executable wrist rotation. Orientation channels use S R S; the native end-effector orientation is unchanged.
action_frame_semantics.future_channels: All future labels are reflected by this same chunk-start s, never a future-state-derived frame. Sampled future channels never select the frame.

training_only_targets.name: future_relations_world
training_only_targets.source: For k=0..15, current D5 obs[t+k+1]: concatenate (pegGrasp-hand)/0.1m and (goal-pegHead)/0.2m. Beyond the final transition, repeat obs[T] for finite padding only. Convert to the chunk-start reflected coordinates in diffusion_targets and append after encoded action4.
training_only_targets.loss: Auxiliary epsilon MSE weight0.15 on channels4:10, divided by6*sum(valid_mask) with a safe zero-valid denominator. Invalid padded elements contribute zero. The host's action epsilon loss remains weight1 and denominator4*sum(valid_mask). At inference these6 channels start from host noise and are sampled jointly; there are no future targets in context and no auxiliary decoding controller.

architecture: Single unchanged factory U-Net with condition_dim50 per observation and diffusion_action_dim10. No additional learned encoder, auxiliary head, planner or support-fit statistics. Deterministic physical-scale feature map and orthogonal involutive action encoding.
support_fit_statistics: None. All target arrays are produced only through training_targets on exact D5; no trajectory or label cache is stored in deployment state.
change_summary: Initial independent design with a contact-conditioned lateral action frame and joint future-geometry diffusion. Unlike A1 it modifies the diffusion variable/frame; unlike A2 it has no learned router or auxiliary regression head. All three scientific designs were specified before any development performance feedback.
